inputs.original_text: Have you heard about these local organizers in southern Alberta collecting signatures to block coal mining under the claim of protecting the watershed? Water Not Coal, started by Corb Lund last month, is pushing a citizen initiative petition to force the Government of Alberta to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration.” This is the usual activist effort to shut down responsible resource development under the banner of environmental protection, placing progressive priorities ahead of the jobs, family stability, and economic strength that coal and energy industries have long provided in Alberta. We need to stand firm for tradition and authority rather than letting these petitions chip away at our ability to manage our own resources.
inputs.modified_text: In southern Alberta, a group called Water Not Coal, founded by Corb Lund only last month, is gathering signatures for a petition designed to make the Government of Alberta “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration.” They are doing this under the pretense of protecting the watershed, but it's really an attempt by activists to halt responsible resource development in the name of the environment. This approach elevates progressive ideas above the jobs, family stability, and economic strength that coal and energy industries have long provided in Alberta. It's vital that we uphold tradition and authority and prevent these kinds of petitions from weakening our control over our own resources.
